questions.question: The present age of a father is three times that of his elder son. Four years hence, the age of the father will be four times that of his younger son. If the difference between the present ages of the elder and younger child is 6 years, what is the present age of the father?
questions.questionHtml: The present age of a father is three times that of his elder son. Four years hence, the age of the father will be four times that of his younger son. If the difference between the present ages of the elder and younger child is 6 years, what is the present age of the father?
questions.solution:
(1) The present age of a father is three times that of his elder son.

Let the present age of father be F and that of elder son's be E, then:

F = 3 × E

(2) Four years hence, the age of the father will be four times that of his younger son.

Let the present age of younger son be Y, then:

F + 4 = 4 × (Y + 4)

(3) If the difference between the present ages of the elder and younger child is 6 years, then:

E - Y = 6 ⇒ E = Y + 6, 

From above three statements,

⇒ F = 3Y + 18 (from (1) and (3))

⇒ Y = (F - 18) ÷ 3

Now, substituting Y in (2)

⇒ \(F + 4 = 4 × [{(F - 18) \over 3} + 4]\)

⇒ \({F\over 4} + 1= {F \over 3} - 6 + 4\)

⇒ \({F \over 3} - {F\over 4} = 3\)

⇒ F = 3 × 12

⇒ F = 36

Hence, the present age of father is 36 years.

questions.question: The ________ rate measures rising prices in everything except food and energy.
questions.questionHtml: The ________ rate measures rising prices in everything except food and energy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is core inflation.

Key Points

  • The core inflation rate measures rising prices in everything except food and energy.
    • The prime rate does not include food and energy prices because they vary greatly each month.
    • This exclusion makes the main rate more accurate than the headline inflation rate in measuring underlying inflationary trends.
    • Headline inflation is the total inflation in an economy. The headline inflation figure includes inflation in a basket of goods that includes items such as food and energy.

Additional Information

  • Stagflation is characterized by slow economic growth and relatively high unemployment. It is caused by cost-push inflation.
  • Wage inflation is an increase in nominal wages which means workers receive higher pay and that tends to cause price inflation.
  • Deflation is when consumer and asset prices decrease over time, and purchasing power increases.

questions.question: Which of the following is also called ‘green algae’?

    • These are organisms characterized by having chlorophyll a and b as the major photosynthetic pigments.

  • Phaeophyceae are brown algae. They live in marine environments, where they play an important role as both food and potential habitat.

options.html: A good that is consumed by a single person or household

options.text: A good that is available to everyone to consume, regardless of who pays for it and who does not.
options.html: A good that is available to everyone to consume, regardless of who pays for it and who does not.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is A good that is consumed by a single person or household.

Key Points

  • A good that is consumed by a single person or household is a private good. 
    • A public good is a product that one individual can consume without reducing its availability to others and from which no one is excluded.
    • A private good is the opposite of a public good.
    • A private good is a product that must be purchased to be consumed, and consumption by one individual prevents another individual from consuming it.
    • We encounter private goods every day. For example- dinner at a restaurant, grocery shopping, airplane rides, and cellphones.
    • Any item that is effectively destroyed or rendered unusable for its original purpose through use, such as food and toilet paper, are also private good.

questions.question: Of the known elements in the periodic table, only _______ are gases under normal atmospheric conditions.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 11.

Key Points

  • Of the known elements in the periodic table, only 11 are gases under normal atmospheric conditions.
    • These gases are hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, fluorine, chlorine, helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon and radon.
    • The periodic table is managed by the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry, or IUPAC.
    • The modern periodic table sorts the elements according to increasing atomic number instead of increasing atomic mass.
    • There are 118 elements in a periodic table.
    • There are seven periods and eighteen groups in the modern periodic table.

Additional Information

  • The size of the atoms (atomic size) decreases as we move from left to right in a period.
  • The metallic properties of elements decrease while the non-metallic properties increase as we move from left to right in a period.
  • Atoms increase in size (or increase in atomic size) as you move down a group of the periodic table.
  • The metallic properties of elements increase as we move down the group of the periodic table.

    • They use complex organic compounds as a source of energy and carbon, not photosynthesis.
    • They are found in almost any habitat, but live mostly on land, primarily on soil or plant material rather than in sea or freshwater.
    • A small number of fungi cause diseases in animals.
    • In humans, fungal diseases include skin diseases such as athlete's foot, ringworm, and thrush.

Additional Information

  • Morphology is the branch of biology that deals with the form of living organisms, and with relationships between their structures.
  • Kalology is the branch of philosophy dealing with taste and the study of beauty in nature and art.
  • Virology is the scientific discipline concerned with the study of the biology of viruses and viral diseases.

    • Transition metal compounds that dissolve in water exhibit a wide variety of bright colors.

questions.question: Radha purchased a Computer table for Rs. 10000 and a Centre table for Rs. 5000. She sold Computer table with 8% profit. With what profit percent should she sell the Centre table so as to gain 10% on the whole transaction.
questions.questionHtml: Radha purchased a Computer table for Rs. 10000 and a Centre table for Rs. 5000. She sold Computer table with 8% profit. With what profit percent should she sell the Centre table so as to gain 10% on the whole transaction.
questions.solution:
Given:

Cost price of a computer table = Rs.10000

Cost price of a centre table = Rs.5000

Profit % for computer table = 8%

Formula:

SP - CP = Profit

Profit % = (SP - CP)/CP × 100

Calculation:

Selling price of a computer table = 10000 × 108/100 = Rs.10800

Total cost price of computer table and centre table = 10000 + 5000 = Rs.15000

Selling price of a computer table and centre table = 15000 × 110/100 = Rs.16500

Selling price of a centre table = 16500 - 10800 = Rs.5700

Profit % when selling price of a centre table = (5700 - 5000)/5000 × 100 = 14%

∴ Profit % for centre table is 14%.

questions.question: A heap of wheat is in the form of a cone whose base diameter is 8.4 m and height is 1.75 m. The heap is to be covered by canvas. What is the area (in m 2 ) of the canvas required? (Use \(\pi=\frac{22}{7} \) )
questions.questionHtml: A heap of wheat is in the form of a cone whose base diameter is 8.4 m and height is 1.75 m. The heap is to be covered by canvas. What is the area (in m2) of the canvas required? (Use \(\pi=\frac{22}{7} \))
questions.solution:
Given:

Diameter of cone = 8.4m

Height of cone = 1.75m

Formula used:

Pythagoras Theorem,

h = \(\sqrt{p^2+b^2}\)

Where, h = hypotenuse, p = perpendicular, and b = Base

The curved surface area of the cone = πrl

Where, l = Slant height, r = Radius

Calculation:

Radius of cone = \(8.4\over2\) = 4.2 m

Using Pythagoras Theorem,

l = \(\sqrt{r^2+h^2}\)

⇒ l = \(\sqrt{4.2^2+1.75^2} \) 

⇒ \(\sqrt{20.7025} \) = 4.55 m

The curved surface area of the cone = πrl

⇒ \(22\over7\) × 4.2 × 4.55

⇒ 60.06 m2 

∴ The area of canvas required is 60.06 m2.

questions.question: Chamanlal, Arshad and Jagit Singh contested an election. All the votes polled were valid. Arshad got 35% of the total votes. For every 35 votes Chamanlal got 14 votes. The winner got 4950 more votes than the person who received the least number of votes. Find the total number of votes polled.
questions.questionHtml: Chamanlal, Arshad and Jagit Singh contested an election. All the votes polled were valid. Arshad got 35% of the total votes. For every 35 votes Chamanlal got 14 votes. The winner got 4950 more votes than the person who received the least number of votes. Find the total number of votes polled.
questions.solution:
Given:

Arshad got = 35% of total votes

Calculation:

Let the total number of votes polled be N.

Arshad got votes = N × 35/100 = 7N/20

Chamanlal got votes = N/35 × 14 = 2N/5

Jagjit got votes = N - 7N/20 - 2N/5 = N/4

Jagjit got less number of votes while Chamanlal won the election.

Then,

⇒ 2N/5 = N/4 + 4950

⇒ N = 33000

∴ Total number of votes polled is 33000.

questions.question: A train leaves station A at 8 am and reaches station B at 12 noon. A car leaves station B at 8:30 am and reaches station A at the same time when the train reaches station B. At what time do they meet?
questions.questionHtml: A train leaves station A at 8 am and reaches station B at 12 noon. A car leaves station B at 8:30 am and reaches station A at the same time when the train reaches station B. At what time do they meet?
questions.solution:
Given:

Train leaves station A at 8am

Train completes journey in 4 hours

Car leaves station B at 8.30am

Car completes journey in 3.5 hours

Formula Used:

Speed = Distance/time

Calculation:

Let the total distance between the two stations be A km

According to the question

Speed of car = \(\frac{2A}{7}\) kmph

Speed of train = \(\frac{A}{4}\) kmph

⇒ Distance covered by train in half-hour = \(\frac{A}{4}\) × \(\frac{1}{2}\) = \(\frac{A}{8}\) km

Remaining distance = A - \(\frac{A}{8}\) = \(\frac{7A}{8}\) km

Let the time after which they meet be B hours

⇒ \(\frac{A\times B}{4}\) + \(\frac{2A\times B}{7}\) = \(\frac{7A}{8}\)

⇒ \(\frac{B}{4}\) + \(\frac{2B}{7}\) = \(\frac{7}{8}\)

⇒ \(\frac{7B+8B}{28}\) = \(\frac{7}{8}\)

⇒ \(\frac{15B}{7}\) = \(\frac{7}{2}\)

⇒ B = \(\frac{49}{30}\) = \(\frac{98}{60}\) = 1 hour 38 minutes

Train will meet car at 8.30 + 1 hour 38 mins = 10.08 am

∴ Train will meet car at 10.08 am.

questions.question: If \(4x^4-37x^2+9=0, x>\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}\) , then what is the value of \(8x^3-\frac{27}{x^3}\)
questions.questionHtml: If \(4x^4-37x^2+9=0, x>\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}\), then what is the value of \(8x^3-\frac{27}{x^3}\)
questions.solution:
Given:

4x4 - 37x2 + 9 = 0 and x > √3/2

Calculation:

⇒ 4x4 - 37x2 + 9 = 0

Let us consider x2 = a,

⇒ 4a2 - 37a + 9 = 0

⇒ 4a2 - 36a - a + 9 = 0

⇒ 4a(a - 9) - 1(a - 9) = 0

⇒ (4a - 1)(a - 9) = 0

a = 1/4 or a = 9

Then,

x2 = 1/4 not acceptable as x > √3/2 means x2 > 3/2 .

x2 = 9 then x = 3 or x = -3 (not valid as x > √3/2)

Then, put x = 3

⇒ ? = 8x3 - 27/x3

⇒ ? = 8 × 33 - 27/33

⇒ ? = 215

∴ 8x3 - 27/x3 = 215

questions.question: A and B can complete a work in 15 days and 10 days respectively. They started doing the work together but after 4 days B had to leave. Then A working with a new worker C completed the remaining work in 3 days. If C works alone, in how many days he can do 40% of the same work?
questions.questionHtml: A and B can complete a work in 15 days and 10 days respectively. They started doing the work together but after 4 days B had to leave. Then A working with a new worker C completed the remaining work in 3 days. If C works alone, in how many days he can do 40% of the same work?
questions.solution:
Given:

A's 1 day's work = 1/15

B's 1 day's work = 1/10

Calculation:

(A + B)'s 1 day's work = 1/15 + 1/10 = 1/6

(A + B)'s 4 days work = 4 × 1/6 = 2/3

Remaining work = 1 - 2/3 = 1/3

Work completed in 3 days by A and C = 1/3 × 1/3 = 1/9

Let C's 1 day's work be 1/C.

⇒ 1/15 + 1/C = 1/9

⇒ 1/C = 2/45

C alone can complete work in = 45/2 days

Time taken by C to complete 40% of work = 40/100 × 45/2 = 9 days

∴ Time taken by C to complete 40% of work is 9 days.

Alternate Method

Hence, C does in 3 days = 30 - (3 + 2) × 4 - (2 × 3) = 4 units

C does = 4/3 units a day

Required days = 30 × 40% ÷ 4/3 = 9 days

∴ Time taken by C to complete 40% of work is 9 days.

The number of days in which person alone can complete work × fraction of work = Time taken by the person to complete a fraction of work.

questions.questionHtml: If \(a-\frac{12}{a}=1\), where a > 0, then the value of \(a^2+\frac{16}{a^2}\) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

By observation, for the equation a − 12/a = 1, let a = 4.

Check: 4 − 12/4 = 4 − 3 = 1 (Condition a > 0 is satisfied).

Substitute a = 4 in the expression a2 + 16/a2.

Value = 42 + 16/42 ⇒ 16 + 16/16 = 16 + 1 = 17.

∴ The correct answer is 17.

Alternate Method

Given: a − 12/a = 1 where a > 0.

Formula Used: Quadratic Equation Factorization.

⇒ a − 12/a = 1

⇒ a2 − 12 = a

⇒ a2 − a − 12 = 0

⇒ a2 − 4a + 3a − 12 = 0

⇒ a(a − 4) + 3(a − 4) = 0

⇒ (a − 4)(a + 3) = 0

⇒ a = 4 or a = −3

⇒ Since a > 0, we take a = 4.

⇒ Required value = a2 + 16/a2

⇒ Value = 42 + 16/42

⇒ Value = 16 + 1 = 17.

∴ The correct answer is 17.

Additional Information

Quadratic Formula

The roots of any quadratic equation ax2 + bx + c = 0 can be found using x = (−b ± √(b2 − 4ac)) / 2a.

Nature of Roots

The term D = b2 − 4ac is called the discriminant. If D > 0, the equation has two distinct real roots.

Algebraic Identities

For problems involving x + 1/x = k, remember that x2 + 1/x2 = k2 − 2. Adjustments must be made if coefficients are unequal.

questions.question: In a triangle ABC, point D lies on AB, and point E and F lies on BC such that DF is parallel to AC and DE is parallel to AF. If BE = 4 cm, CF = 3 cm, then find the length (in cm) of EF.

questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In this configuration where DF || AC and DE || AF, the segments on the base follow a geometric progression property.

Using the Basic Proportionality Theorem twice, we derive: BF2 = BE × BC.

Let EF = x cm. Then BF = 4 + x and BC = 4 + x + 3 = 7 + x.

⇒ (4 + x)2 = 4 × (7 + x)

⇒ 16 + x2 + 8x = 28 + 4x ⇒ x2 + 4x − 12 = 0

⇒ (x + 6)(x − 2) = 0 ⇒ x = 2 (since length cannot be negative).

∴ The correct answer is 2 cm.

Alternate Method

Key Points

  • For converting the active voice into passive voice, the following steps should be taken:-
  • The subject 'the postman' of the active voice becomes the object of the passive voice.
  • The object 'the letter' of the active voice becomes the subject of the passive voice. 
  • The tense(past perfect tense) changes according to the following structure:-
    • Active Voice - Subject + had + V3 + Object.
    • Passive Voice - Object + had + been + V3 + Subject.
  • Thus, the correct answer is Option 3.

  • हमें इसे passive voice में बदलने की जरूरत है।

  • Active voice का subject 'the postman' passive voice का object बन जाता है।
  • Active voice का ऑब्जेक्ट 'the letter' passive voice का subject बन जाता है।
  • निम्नलिखित संरचना के अनुसार काल (past perfect tense) बदल जाता है:-
